extracted.intended_audience: readers of The Popular Science Monthly — educators, teachers of cookery, housekeepers, and general educated readers interested in science, domestic economy, and textbook/manual quality
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and standards for assessing cookbooks, cookery training-schools, and related educational manuals (also a few criteria for scientific textbooks and field guides) — emphasises practical teaching, clarity, and suitability to audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Origin in teaching / practice-tested content
rubrics_metrics.description: The hand-book required to teach cookery effectually cannot be made by any single person in the usual manner, but it must be itself a product of such teaching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The volume should 'embody[] a tried and successful method of making good practical cooks.' Lessons and receipts must have been elaborated in a training-kitchen, repeatedly practised and revised under critical direction so that instructions reflect the accumulated experience of teaching beginners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plainness and simplicity for self-education
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the 'plainest, simplest, and most perfect guide to self-education in the kitchen' and is republished for use by American families for self-instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receipts should be homely, direct, and meant to be easily and distinctly understood rather than literary or entertaining; the book should be usable by persons of common sense who desire to learn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate selection of dishes for varied economic needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Dishes have been chosen 'to meet the needs of well-to-do families, and also those of more moderate means, who must observe a strict economy.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an ample and varied diet while including simple, frugal meals and economical alternatives; avoid costly artistic refinements while maintaining simple good taste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching method superiority (minute, explicit, complete instructions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'especial merit' is the superior method of teaching practical cookery: directions are minute, explicit, distinct, and complete so they may be followed with ease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each recipe should be a lesson in a practical process: steps separated and given in numerical order; precautions against mistakes; repetition where processes recur; the aim is to teach methods, not merely list recipes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on practice (hands-on instruction over mere exposition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mere exposition and illustration are wholly inadequate; a cooking school, to be thorough, must provide for practice; lecturing and showing alone will fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructional materials and courses must form classes to perform the work themselves; cooking (like music) can only be learned by actually doing it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete lesson sheets: ingredients, quantities, costs, and ordered operations
rubrics_metrics.description: For each lesson pupils were furnished with a printed sheet stating ingredients, the quantities and separate cost of these ingredients, what was to be done first, what next, and so on through the whole series of operations, nothing being assumed as known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipes and lesson sheets should list ingredient amounts and individual costs, and provide a chronological sequence of operations that assumes no prior knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterative revision and incorporation of classroom experience
rubrics_metrics.description: These guides were necessarily imperfect at first and were subject to constant revision and extension as experience suggested corrections; at each printing the improvements that had been made were incorporated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructional texts should be refined over multiple editions based on learner mistakes, teacher observations, and repeated class trials; treat the book as a living product of instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate and prevent learner mistakes (robust troubleshooting)
rubrics_metrics.description: The precautions against mistakes are so careful that even the dullest can hardly go wrong; completeness of the instructions was attained through the stupidities, blunders, mistakes, questionings and difficulties of hundreds of learners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include warnings, common failure modes, and step-by-step safeguards so that beginners can avoid typical errors; don't assume tacit knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attention to minutiae and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The excellence of these lessons consists in their faithfulness in regard to minutias, and the habits they enforce of attention to trifling particulars. Slight mistakes, small omissions, little things done at the wrong time, spoil dishes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stress exact timing, small details, and order of operations; explicit repetition of small but crucial steps is desirable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional, kitchen-oriented presentation over literary style
rubrics_metrics.description: The receipts are not enticing reading, because they were made to work by. The book, in fact, belongs in the kitchen where cookery is done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize practical clarity and repeatability rather than elegant prose; expect and permit repetition and plain phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include authoritative dietetic guidance linked to cookery
rubrics_metrics.description: Appended is an admirable essay on 'The Principles of Diet in Health and Disease'... an authoritative summary of the facts and rules of the most recent dietetical science. As food is prepared to be eaten, cookery is in close relations with diet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good cookery manuals should include or be complemented by sound dietary principles so readers can connect preparation with nutrition and health.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not assume reading-alone suffices for practical arts
rubrics_metrics.description: Popular manuals proceed upon the false principle that a practical vocation... can be learned by simply reading about it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design manuals and courses to include practice opportunities; avoid formats that only describe processes without enabling hands-on learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lesson structure: separate steps and numeric ordering
rubrics_metrics.description: The steps are separated, and given in numerical order, so as to enforce attention to one thing at a time, and the right thing at the right time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure each recipe/lesson as discrete, ordered tasks to simplify attention and execution for learners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and curation for collections (essays/current discussion)
rubrics_metrics.description: The collection gives a judicious selection of the most important papers that have appeared in the English reviews by distinguished writers; brought out in a neat and attractive shape by the publishers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors of essay collections should select significant contemporary pieces by reputable authors and present them attractively and accessibly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Science annuals: prioritize comprehensive summaries over exhaustive abstracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Omitting abstracts of notable scientific papers enables more space and fuller treatment to the 'Summary of Scientific Progress,' resulting in a remarkably satisfactory review of the year's work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual compendia should consider focusing on authoritative, readable summaries of progress in each field, written by eminent specialists, rather than attempting to compress long papers into brief abstracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Textbook pedagogy for complex subjects (start simple, build complexity)
rubrics_metrics.description: To avoid complication we deal with the simplest motions first, and gradually go on to consider the more complex ones; postpone consideration of changes in size and shape by treating only of rigid bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mathematical and scientific texts should define terms clearly, begin with the simplest cases, and progressively introduce complexity to fix ideas before formal generalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical science manuals: experiment construction, low-cost apparatus, and illustrative experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Manual contains valuable practical instruction for making experiments in physics: manipulation of apparatus, construction of apparatus at the least possible cost, points to be considered in purchase of instruments; directions for experiments illustrating principal laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Books for teachers and students should provide clear instructions for building and using affordable apparatus, guidance on purchasing instruments, and step-by-step experiments that illustrate core physical laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field guide standards: locality info, identification keys, cultivation and preservation advice, illustrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Guide to principal localities where ferns occur, and a key for determining different species; contains hints on cultivation and on proper method of drying and preserving them, plus etchings and woodcuts to illustrate species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regional natural history guides should combine locality guidance, identification keys, cultivation/preservation instructions, and quality illustrations to support collectors and amateur naturalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational outcome criterion for classical studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Classical studies should not merely drill grammar and dates; they should produce critical familiarity with Latin and Greek vocabularies, a conception of the thought of the ancients so as to see how we are their intellectual descendants, and a sound historical training rather than rote memorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessments of classical curricula should look for deep engagement, historical perspective, and enduring interest that students sustain into later life, rather than mere rote learning or detriment to mastery of the mother tongue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curricular balance recommendation (reduce classics, increase math/physical sciences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Professor Du Bois-Reymond urges that 'Classical studies... should be retrenched in the gymnasia, and greater attention given to mathematics and the physical sciences.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where classical instruction fails to yield critical historical and linguistic competency and impedes native-language mastery, consider rebalancing secondary curricula toward mathematics and physical sciences.
